articles.title: Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest: Victor Munoz equalises as Andoni Iraola's first Anfield Premier League game ends in a draw
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Victor Munoz scores a second equaliser of the afternoon for Liverpool against Nottingham Forest; Alexander Isak had earlier cancelled out Dan Ndoye's opener before Morgan Gibbs-White scored a penalty following Alisson's foul on Neco Williams
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola was heading towards defeat in his first Anfield Premier League game in charge of Liverpool when Morgan Gibbs-White converted a debatable penalty with 20 minutes to play.

Liverpool's frustration was only heightened by an issue with the fourth official's electronic board seemingly delaying the manager's planned substitutions in the build up to the spot-kick.

Latest news and rumours: Liverpool | Forest

But summer signing Munoz put an otherwise frustrating first appearance in front of his new home fans behind him with an emphatic equaliser.

A first win with Liverpool still remains elusive for Iraola, having seen his side also come from behind to draw 2-2 at Newcastle last weekend. He will hope the seemingly imminent arrival of £120m Bradley Barcola can kickstart their season.

Winger Munoz had moved to the right flank just a few minutes before his strike, after Cody Gakpo, who had impressed on that side despite transfer links with Tottenham and Man City, was subbed off. The Dutchman's low cross through the six-yard box had been tapped in by the otherwise anonymous Alexander Isak earlier in the second half as Liverpool put a poor first 45 behind them.

Iraola's side struggled to deal with the direct approach of Forest for much of that opening period, with a long ball from Matz Sels proving their undoing in the build-up to Dan Ndoye's opener.

The defending from Liverpool for that goal was poor but Forest boss Oliver Glasner will ultimately rue missed chances in that half, with a stunning stop from Alisson just before half-time to push Igor Jesus' shot onto the bar proving key.

It was an entertaining, action-packed draw - but a frustrating one for both sides, who continue to look for their first league wins of the season.

12: BLOCK! Dan Ndoye nods down Ola Aina's back-post cross but Igor Jesus' attempt to turn it in is blocked by a big stretch from Liverpool centre-back Jeremy Jacquet!

19: CLOSE! Ndoye meets James McAtee's cute, clipped cross at the back post but steers his header across goal and wide of the other stick.

24: GOAL! Ndoye finishes across Alisson after Jesus latches onto a long ball from Matz Sels and feeds Morgan Gibbs-White to find Ndoye in the box.

33: GOAL RULED OUT! Florian Wirtz thinks he's pulled Liverpool level after intercepting a McAtee pass and converting from Jeremie Frimpong's pass - but a VAR check judged Frimpong offside before he made the assist.

39: WHAT A SAVE! Cody Gakpo crosses from the right but Wirtz's good header is tipped over the bar by Sels.

45: OVER! Munoz bends one narrowly over the bar! He had to hit the target.

60: GOAL! Alexander Isak taps in Gakpo's low cross from close range to equalise.

70: GOAL! Gibbs-White sends Alisson the wrong way with a penalty to restore Forest's lead after the goalkeeper brought down Neco Williams after a quick throw from Liam Delap.

82: GOAL! Munoz thumps in an equaliser off the underside of the bar, with the help of a deflection off Murillo. Wirtz with the pass into him and the assist.

85: CLOSE! Dominik Szoboszlai so close to a free-kick winner but whips his shot past the post.

Analysis: Was the Forest penalty call correct?

"He's knocked it over the goalkeeper and Alisson has caught him slightly.

"There's not much else he can do. It's like a coming together.

"But once it's given, it's not going to be overturned because it's not a clear and obvious error from the referee."

"I just thought it was a shot going wide. It's harsh. I don't think there's a lot of contact.

"There's nothing he can do. He's coming out to get the ball."

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola to TNT Sports:

"Not the result you want. Two very different halves. We were poor in the first half. Even being unlucky with their goal slightly VAR offside, the goal we score is slightly offside.

"The intensity was different [in the second half]. A lot more intense, a lot more threatening. I was happy with the second half but it was late for winning the game.

"First half has been poor, it's definitely not good enough. When you go 1-1 the momentum is with you. We concede another one and everything becomes difficult. And we couldn't finish the comeback."

Analysis: Will Liverpool cash in on in-form Gakpo?

Cody Gakpo has attracted interest from Tottenham and Man City and with Deadline Day fast approaching his future is far from certain. The impending arrival of Bradley Barcola has also fuelled talk that the Dutchman will be heading for the exit.

But at the same time, Gakpo has been one of Liverpool's best performers during their stuttering start to the season. He scored at Newcastle last weekend and could have had more. On Saturday he put Isak's goal on a plate with a sumptuous cross after getting in down the right.

The switch of flanks from his favoured left side didn't deter him and he was Liverpool's brightest spark during the first half when they otherwise struggled. That versatility is a trait which is important to Iraola with the way he likes his wingers to operate.

This early-season good form from Gakpo, though, could soon be continued in a different club's shirt, should Liverpool receive an offer and opt to cash-in before 11pm on Tuesday. His impactful performances could convince his admirers to make their bid.

Glasner: Proud of performance, disappointed with result

"Overall the performance was top, especially first half, creating so many chances here at Anfield. I really loved the reaction after we conceded the equaliser, we still played forward and were rewarded with the penalty.

"We feel proud of the performance - but also disappointed with the result. This tells us a lot. A lot of positives to take but still a lot of work to do."

articles.title: Bill Belichick Reportedly Set to Call UNC's Defensive Plays vs. TCU Amid Son Steve's Absence
articles.summary: University of North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick is reportedly expected to be the defensive play-caller during the Tar Heels' season-opening game against TCU in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday.
articles.body:
University of North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick is reportedly expected to be the defensive play-caller during the Tar Heels' season-opening game against TCU in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday.

According to On3.com's Pete Nakos , Belichick collaborated with defensive line coach Bob Diaco on a defensive gameplan, and Belichick will call the plays in the absence of his son and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick.

On Aug. 6, Bill announced that Steve was being placed on indefinite medical leave, and he did not provide a timeline for Steve's return.

This marks Belichick's second season as the head coach at UNC after making the leap from the NFL. He went 4-8 during his first campaign at the helm.

The 74-year-old Belichick is widely regarded as one of the best head coaches and defensive minds in NFL history, as he won six Super Bowls as head coach of the New England Patriots and two Super Bowls as the New York Giants' defensive coordinator.

Steve Belichick joined his father's coaching staff in New England as a defensive assistant in 2012 and later served as a safeties coach, defensive backs coach and outside linebackers coach. He also took over as the Pats' defensive play-caller in 2019.

After Bill Belichick and the Patriots decided to part ways at the conclusion of the 2023 season, Steve spent 2024 with the Washington Commanders as their defensive coordinator and outside linebackers coach.

Bill took 2024 off from coaching before accepting the head coaching job at UNC for the 2025 campaign.

With Steve as his DC, Bill did not have much success during his debut season with the Tar Heels, as they went just 2-6 in ACC play and missed out on playing in a bowl game for the first time since 2018.

Bill will look to get off to a better start this year against TCU, but he won't have his son to lean on in key defensive situations.

articles.standfirst: Mantendrá al extremo verdiblanco entre seis y ocho semanas en el dique seco

articles.title: Daniel Munoz: Nottingham Forest agree deal to sign Crystal Palace defender
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest agree a deal worth a minimum of £22m to sign Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth a minimum of £22m to sign Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace .

The Colombia international has now been given permission to have a medical before joining Forest.

The deal will reunite Munoz with Forest boss Oliver Glasner, who worked with the full-back during his time in charge at Selhurst Park.

Talks over the move have been ongoing for several days and accelerated after Palace's 4-1 defeat by Manchester City on Friday.

Munoz joined Palace from Belgian side Genk in 2024 and has been a key player for the Eagles in recent seasons, playing a crucial part in the club's historic FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs under Glasner.

The 30-year-old has just under two years left on his current deal and Palace are prepared to sell this summer.

Palace signed Anan Khalaili from Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise earlier this summer and the Israel international is expected to take Munoz's place in Pierre Sage's team.

Munoz has made 109 appearances for Palace, scoring 11 goals, and played in their opening 2-0 Premier League defeat at Everton . However, he was an unused subsitute in the loss to City.

Forest have also launched an ambitious bid - £40m plus a potential sell-on clause - to sign Everton 's teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong.

articles.title: El Elversberg debuta en Bundesliga tumbando al nuevo Leverkusen de Carles Martínez
articles.standfirst: Hace cuatro años estaban en Cuarta división... y derrotaron (3-2) al único campeón invicto en la historia de la máxima categoría del fútbol alemán
articles.summary: Hace cuatro años estaban en Cuarta división... y derrotaron (3-2) al único campeón invicto en la historia de la máxima categoría del fútbol alemán
articles.body: En 2022, el Elversberg militaba en Cuarta división alemana. Cuatro años después, les tocaba debutar en Bundesliga ante el Bayer Leverkusen, el único campeón invicto en la historia de la competición... y han sacado los tres puntos (3-2) con un equipo de apenas 24.7 años de media en el que Ole Book, actual director deportivo del Borussia Dortmund, sentó las bases. Carles Martínez Novell firma un estreno para olvidar. Ya sin Exequiel Palacios en plantilla, transferido al Ipswich Town tras más de seis años en el club, 'Equi' Fernández ejerció como pareja de Aleix García en la medular de un Bayer Leverkusen con marcado acento español en los lateral: Lucas Vázquez en derecha y Miguel Gutiérrez en izquierda. No había libre ni una de las 10.000 localidades que componen el Ursapharm-Arena. Nadie en Elversberg (población de 13.000 habitantes) quería perderse el estreno de su equipo en la máxima categoría del fútbol alemán. Ahora bien, lo que pocos podían intuir es que, en menos de 10', iban a estar 2-0 arriba en el marcador. Francis Onyeka, cedido por el propio Bayer Leverkusen, fue el autor de la asistencia en favor de Lukas Petkov que definió con la zurda desde la corona del área. Le mató el paso en falso a un Mark Flekken que tampoco estuvo acertado en la siguiente acción. Tras el saque de centro, Tapsoba regaló el balón, Cole Campbell remató centrado... y se le escapó de las manos. Aleix García retrasó unos metros su posición, Miguel Gutiérrez metió algún envío desde el costado izquierdo, Maza trató de crear superioridades por dentro... Pero la realidad es que el Leverkusen tampoco incomodó al Elversberg a lo largo de todo el primer tiempo. La más clara la tuvo el propio Aleix con una falta lejana que se estrelló en el larguero tras tocar en un hombre de la barrera. Necesitaba empezar a despertar el Bayer Leverkusen si quería darle la vuelta a la situación tras el descanso. Pero, nada más ponerse el balón en juego, el Elversberg volvió a hacer saltar todo por los aires. Recogió Petkov un envío de Onyenka desde izquierda y volvió a meter un balón al corazón del área transformado por un Mokwa que le comió la tostada a Badé. No le hizo falta ver más a Carles Martínez para 'revolucionar' el equipo con un triple cambio antes del 55'. Entraron Quansah, 'Facu' Medina y Kofane para instalar una línea de tres atrás, como solía hacer en el Toulouse, donde Afonso Moreira y Miguel Gutiérrez se ubicaron como carrileros. Ni por esas parecía reaccionar un Bayer Leverkusen que seguía sin rematar a puerta. El primero llegó cuando ya restaban menos de 15' para el final del partido... y acabó dentro. Disparó Maza entre un mar de piernas desde la frontal y Schick desvió lo justo para cambiar la trayectoria. Se vino arriba el Leverkusen y, ya en el descuento, Kofane marcó el 3-2 recogiendo un remate al larguero de un repatriado Boniface. Hofmann llegó a rozar el empate... pero la suerte acabó sonriendo al Elversberg. No lo tendrán fácil para mantener la categoría. Pero, pase lo que pase, este día ya quedará para la historia del club.

articles.title: Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest: Andoni Iraola frustrated by long wait to make substitutions
articles.summary: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he was angry about being prevented from making a triple substitution sooner during his side's draw against Nottingham Forest.
articles.body:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he was angry about being prevented from making a triple substitution sooner during Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw against Nottingham Forest .

With the game level at 1-1 during the second half at Anfield, the Basque wanted to bring on Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha.

However, despite the ball going out of play three times, the players were left waiting on the sideline as fourth official Tim Robinson had problems with the board.

To add to Liverpool 's frustrations, the third time the ball went out, instead of play stopping for the changes, Forest took a quick throw-in from which they won a penalty to retake the lead.

Forest wing-back Neco Williams darted in behind the Liverpool backline and was caught by goalkeeper Alisson as he lifted a shot goalwards.

When it drifted wide, referee Samuel Barrott blew his whistle and pointed to the spot.

"With the penalty, the situation has already finished when the contact appears. And it's not an aggressive contact," Iraola told BBC Match of the Day.

"But more than this we complained about the subs. We had to wait about three minutes.

"He was having an issue with the board, I don't know if it was not working, but we definitely wanted to do the subs the last two or three stoppages before the goal.

"It wasn't just that reason but everything helps."

Speaking to TNT Sports, he added: "A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes. We'd already given him the subs two or three minutes before.

"I was already angry because in the previous stoppage we couldn't make the subs and then before throw-in I thought we could do it.

"I don't know, they will have to explain it. But it has taken ages."

'That trust isn't there' - how does Iraola get best out of Isak?

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard believed they could have no complaints over the award of the penalty itself but empathised with Iraola's anger over the substitutes.

"You can understand the frustration - in this day and age, with all the technology, it can't be taking three minutes to make a triple substitution," he told TNT Sports.

"But I think it's a small problem in the overall problem because it's a goal that can be avoided."

Ex- Liverpool and England full-back Stephen Warnock agreed with his old team-mate.

"Andoni Iraola wanted to make a triple change and the assistant referee hasn't got the thing done," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"It would've completely stopped the play. It's appalling from the fourth official."

Liverpool were able to salvage a point from the game as Victor Munoz scored his first goal for the club with eight minutes remaining.

articles.summary: El delantero se ejercitó este sábado en El Cerro mientras sus compañeros viajaban a Sevilla y se le espera como uno más en el próximo entrenamiento del Atlético
articles.body: con el cierre del mercado a las 23.59 horas del próximo martes aproximándose y asumido que su "sueño" de jugar en el Barcelona la próxima temporada no tiene una sola posibilidad de cumplirse, Julián Alvarez vuelve a 'pensar' en rojiblanco. No en vano, como ya hiciera en la tarde del viernes, ha vuelto a ejercitarse en la mañana de este sábado en el Cerro junto a uno de los preparadores físicos del club, mientras sus compañeros viajaban a Sevilla para afrontar la visita al Pizjuán de esta noche. De este modo, el argentino ya está listo para reintegrarse al grupo en el próximo entrenamiento, fijado en principio para el domingo. Una aparente vuelta a la normalidad, superada la 'indisposición' que le llevó a ausentarse del trabajo el miércoles y el jueves, que si bien no zanja por completo la incertidumbre que rodea a su futuro, sí supone una señal de que, de momento, la única alternativa al Atlético, que no es otra que la Premier, sigue sin llenarle en absoluto. De ahí que mientras se estrecha el cerco para tomar una decisión definitiva, la Araña haya vuelto a afrontar su realidad como jugador rojiblanco. Por eso, tras seguir un plan personalizado en solitario durante dos días, a Julián ya se le espera para ser uno más a las órdenes de Simeone en la siguiente sesión, previsiblemente mañana domingo, a sólo dos días de que se dé carpetazo definitivamente a su culebrón con el cierre del mercado. En este sentido, certificada su disponibilidad para reintegrarse al grupo con normalidad, desde el Atlético no quieren dejar pasar más tiempo para empezar a 'recuperar' a su estrella si finalmente permanece en el equipo. Una continuidad, por otro lado, a la que el delantero se vería obligado mientras no cambie su postura de que es el Barcelona el único club al que le gustaría salir y su negativa a volver a la Premier por más que el Arsenal y el Manchester City estén dispuestos a abrirle las puertas. No obstante, sin nadie capaz de poner la mano en el fuego ante lo que pueda pasar por la cabeza de Julián en los próximos días, la única realidad es que a día de hoy sigue contando como uno más del Atlético.

El propio Tiago Gomis dejó su sitio a un Christopher Nkunku que recibió una sonora ovación por parte del RB Arena. No tardó en corresponder el francés sirviendo el 3-0 en favor de Roco Reitz en el primer balón que tocó. Pidió disculpas el mediocentro alemán a la que, hasta hace no muchos meses, era su afición. Otro que se reestrenó con el Leipzig tras militar cedido en el Olympique de Marsella durante la última temporada fue Arthur Vermeeren. articles.summary: El Celta viene de una derrota con sorpresa en Balaídos y el Athletic, con líos internos, no ha sumado todavía
articles.body: Balaídos quiere equipos con voces. De esos que gritan sus alegrías en el campo…algo que no hacen Celta y Athletic. Los celestes, que miran ya a su debut en Europa, rascaron un empate sin goles en Valencia y cayeron con sorpresa ante Osasuna. Poco que cantar, la verdad. Pero peor le va al Athletic, con dos derrotas consecutivas y la plantilla de espaldas al presidente por una acumulación de diferencias. Los jugadores han ido a más y viven 'silenzio stampa' para mostrar su enfado. La protesta corre riesgos porque se hace sin puntos y eso no es buena herramienta para la paciencia de los aficionados. Busca el Celta su primera victoria de la temporada y no firmar un comienzo liguero como el de hace un año, pese a la clasificación final, y que así no se reaparezcan los fantasmas en Balaídos. Con una plantilla en la que alguno de sus componentes sigue pendiente del cierre del mercado, Claudio Giráldez volverá a mover un once en el que no podrán estar Marcos Alonso, sancionado, ni Borja Iglesias, lesionado. Dos bajas sensibles. El futbolista del filial, Quique Ribes, es la novedad en la convocatoria. Terzic recupera a Yuri tras su curiosa sanción en el Camp Nou después de que el CTA admitiera que estuvo mal expulsado frente al Sevilla. El alemán volverá a hacer cambios porque quiere un equipo fresco para potenciar la presión alta y, a poder ser, alegre a la hora de construir y decidir en el último tercio del campo. Las variaciones llegarán en todas las líneas. Quizá Areso y Gerenabarrena vuelvan a tener oportunidad de salida después de haber arrancado en el banquillo frente al Barcelona. Cuando la clasificación aprieta los ojos se van derechos a la portería. Y Celta y Athletic tienen buenas herramientas para considerar que saldrán adelante. Radu fue un baluarte olívico el pasado curso y ahora quiere seguir creciendo. Simón viene de hacer una excelente actuación en el Camp Nou. El campeón del mundo con España es garantía. “Un líder, pero queremos que participe lo menos posible”, dice Terzic.

articles.title: Alexander Isak: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola must get best out of striker
articles.summary: Alexander Isak scored his first goal of the season in the 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest - but how do Liverpool get the best out of him?
articles.body:
During Liverpool 's negotiations with Paris St-Germain for Bradley Barcola, the Anfield hierarchy were determined not to pay more than the club-record £125m they spent on Alexander Isak last summer.

When the £123m deal for Barcola is completed over the coming days, the France winger will become the 10th £100m player in Premier League history.

None have cost more than Isak, so the expectation on the former Newcastle striker is understandable, to say the least.

Isak scored 44 Premier League goals in his last two seasons at Newcastle , but in an injury-plagued first campaign at Anfield the 26-year-old found the back of the net just three times in 14 top-flight appearances.

For Andoni Iraola, who has drawn his first two games as Liverpool manager, a major part of success at Anfield will be the ability to get the best out of Isak, who - despite scoring - was largely ineffective in their 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Unlike last summer, Isak has looked sharp in pre-season after some impressive displays for Sweden at the World Cup, but struggled on his return to Tyneside last weekend.

For 45 minutes against Forest on Saturday, those struggles continued with just six touches, one accurate pass and zero shots.

"It is clear that Liverpool haven't worked out how to play with Alexander Isak yet," said ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart, who is a pundit on Saturday's Match of the Day.

"At Newcastle everything flowed through him. That was down to a trust thing that they had built up over time - their midfield knew exactly where he was and they didn't even need to look up as he'd be there waiting.

"At Liverpool that trust just isn't there at the moment - no-one is feeling it and he isn't that central point, which is leading to him looking lost and isolated."

Gibbs-White shines - player ratings for Liverpool v Nottm Forest

Iraola angry as official's board delays subs before goal

It would have been intriguing to be a fly on the wall in the directors' box at Anfield.

Iraola's first home Premier League game was watched by incoming Liverpool vice-chairman Amit Bhatia, principal owner John Henry, and sporting director Richard Hughes, who was integral in getting the deal for Isak done last summer.

Thankfully for them - and Iraola - Isak got Liverpool on level terms after the break. He managed just seven more touches in the second half but centre-forwards deal in goals and the Swede timed his run perfectly to meet Cody Gakpo's delivery for his first goal of the season. His smile after told a story in itself.

"That's the job ultimately as a striker [to score goals]. I am very happy to score the first one and hopefully it just keeps coming," Isak told TNT Sports.

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard described the goal as "big" - for both the striker's confidence and the team's.

But, in Hart's opinion, Iraola still has a major conundrum.

"Andoni Iraola has some big decisions to make," said Hart. "Does he base his team round him [Isak] or does he try to find a different solution within his squad? In my opinion he's got to commit to what the club have done by investing so heavily in Isak.

"There's no point signing these players if you aren't going to use them properly and play to their strengths. There's no doubting Isak's quality - they are just at a bit of a crossroads at the moment."

During Isak's struggles last season, the belief inside the club was that he was a long-term signing and judgement would be reserved for once he was fully fit.

Only Erling Haaland, Mohamed Salah and Ollie Watkins have scored more Premier League goals since Isak's first season in England and, with Salah now out of the picture, the onus is on Isak to deliver - particularly with Hugo Ekitike out injured.

Liverpool 's first two games of the season have finished 2-2 despite Iraola's side enjoying 60% of possession against Newcastle last week and 70% against Forest.

In both games, they have found themselves trailing and are yet to be ahead in the Premier League this season.

That has inevitably made things trickier for Isak, who was such a force in a counter-attacking Newcastle side. Against low blocks, the proposition is different.

It is also symptomatic of a wider issue Iraola faces.

Last season, his Bournemouth side won just four of the 19 Premier League games in which they had the majority of possession. They won nine of the other 19.

The Cherries, who were known for their counter-pressing style and effectiveness in transition, also failed to win a game in which they had more than 58.8% possession.

In essence, his side were more successful when they had less of the ball - something that will rarely happen now he is at Anfield.

"As an attacking force it isn't flowing for Liverpool ," said Hart. "With the physical nature of the Premier League and with them not 100% sure on what they are doing at the moment, teams are stomping all over them.

"It's going to take a whole lot of work from Iraola and his staff on the training pitch, but he is a top coach and they have top players."

Asked about whether he sets targets for the season, Isak said: "Not really. I think every striker wants to score [in] every game he plays. Obviously that's difficult but [we take] each game at a time."

That is one way to look at it, and this was certainly an improvement on his showing against Newcastle , but deep down Isak will know he can - and must - do better.

articles.title: ‘A little jealous’: Sunil Chhetri on India’s chance to play Brazil, Uruguay in friendlies
articles.summary: Football News: NEW DELHI: Former India captain Sunil Chhetri has admitted he feels “a little jealous” watching the current generation get an opportunity to face foot.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India captain Sunil Chhetri has admitted he feels “a little jealous” watching the current generation get an opportunity to face footballing giants Brazil and Uruguay, revealing that he never got such a chance during his long international career.India are scheduled to host five-time world champions Brazil on October 3 and Uruguay three days later at Kolkata’s Salt Lake Stadium. The high-profile fixtures will give a young Indian side a rare opportunity to test itself against two of South America's biggest footballing nations.“I feel a little jealous as a spectator. In my 24-26 years as a professional and nearly 20 years with the national team, I never got an opportunity like this,” Chhetri told the All India Football Federation (AIFF).The former striker, who retired from international football last year, urged the current players to stay fit, compete with determination and make the most of the opportunity. Despite being away from the national-team setup, Chhetri said he remained confident in the squad's young talent.“This is their time. There are so many talented youngsters in the team. Everyone gets their opportunity; just like I got mine 20 years ago,” he said.Chhetri backs coach, rules out comebackChhetri also refused to second-guess the coaching staff when asked about selection decisions and the omission of certain players, insisting that the coach was best placed to assess the team's requirements.“The coach has to answer that. I'm just a fan now, watching like everyone else,” he said.The 42-year-old, who recently returned to training, also dismissed any immediate prospect of making a comeback with a touch of humour.“I just trained for 20 minutes. I'm around 42 now, I can barely run properly and I'm struggling,” he joked.The Brazil and Uruguay fixtures come at a difficult time for Indian football, with the side currently ranked 138th in the FIFA rankings and uncertainty surrounding the domestic calendar. Chhetri, however, called for optimism and collective responsibility rather than a blame game.“The Indian football graph, for as many years as I’ve played, has always been like this. We’re probably in a phase where things are not going very well, because of what we’ve done with the national team, what we’ve done in the league, etcetera. But we all have to be hopeful,” he said on the sidelines of the Football Players' Association of India's Indian Football Awards 2026.“At the end of the day, it’s going to be fine. It takes time. Looking at all your faces, we all want things to be fine as soon as possible. It will be. I’m always hopeful. Things might be a little bit 'kharab' (bad), but things are going to be fine.”Chhetri also accepted that players must take responsibility for the team's struggles.“I was also a part of the national team. And why has the ranking gone down? It’s because of the way we have played, the games that we should have won but lost. That is the reason why we are where we are. As players, we take responsibility. articles.body:
Jayden Daniels enters his third NFL season carrying immense fantasy upside, looking to bounce back after a slew of injuries completely derailed his 2025 campaign. We already know exactly what the ceiling looks like when he is fully healthy: he finished as a top-5 fantasy quarterback in 2024, and he gave us a bit of everything in the process.

Should I Draft Jayden Daniels in Fantasy Football?

To help ensure he reaches that ceiling again, Washington aggressively upgraded his supporting cast this offseason. They added veteran Stefon Diggs, finally giving Daniels reliable wide receiver depth to work with next to Terry McLaurin.

Diggs was managed last season, but he did earn work when on the field and bringing him in allows them to slow play the development of Antonio Williams.

They also brought in Chig Okonkwo from Tennessee to replace Zach Ertz at tight end. I don't think that move was given nearly enough flowers when it happened, as Okonkwo's athleticism over the middle of the field should help elevate the weekly floor of this entire passing unit.

Speaking of floor elevators, running back Rachaad White will play his age-27 season with the Commanders. He caught 40-of-45 targets last season with the Buccaneers and can be considered an absolute elite threat as a pass catcher out of the backfield, giving Daniels a highly reliable check-down option.

I do worry slightly about the overall pass-catcher depth behind Diggs if injuries strike the receiver room. However, if the top few options can simply stay healthy and this coaching staff can maximize what White does out of the backfield, Daniels could not just return to the elite dual-threat production we saw from him in 2024, but potentially improve upon it.

Draft him with confidence. You don't need to draft a backup QB for any of the elites at the position: there is enough depth that you can patchwork the position together should an injury derail this profile for a second straight season.

articles.title: Gladbach's Hashioka taken to hospital after collision in match
articles.summary: New Borussia Mönchengladbach signing Daiki Hashioka was taken to hospital after a collision during the 3-0 defeat at RB Leipzig in their Bundesliga opener on...
articles.body:
New Borussia Mönchengladbach signing Daiki Hashioka was taken to hospital after a collision during the 3-0 defeat at RB Leipzig in their Bundesliga opener on Saturday.

The Japan defender, who suffered pain in the neck area, was carried off on a stretcher.

"He is a tough guy. We really have to be careful, especially in that area. He was immobilized immediately. Now we are hoping it all turns out well," Gladbach sporting director Rouven Schröder told reporters.

The 27-year-old collided with Leipzig's Antonio Nusa in the 72nd minute. The Norwegian was booked for the incident.

articles.title: Updated Caleb Williams Fantasy Outlook 2026: Bears QB Looks to Take Chicago to the Promise Land
articles.summary: Caleb Williams enters the 2026 fantasy football season primed for another step forward, with all signs pointing toward a monster campaign as he fully masters...
articles.body:
Caleb Williams enters the 2026 fantasy football season primed for another step forward, with all signs pointing toward a monster campaign as he fully masters this Ben Johnson offensive scheme. Last year, he nearly became the first quarterback in Bears history to throw for 4,000 yards, and we already know what he offers on the ground after he ran for nearly 500 yards as a rookie.

Should I Draft Caleb Williams in Fantasy Football?

When evaluating the ceiling of Williams, he simply has as many levers as anyone to pull when it comes to piling up fantasy points in a hurry. Including the postseason, he ended last year by logging seven straight multi-pass TD games. Furthermore, he recorded nine games last season with a 10+ yard rush, establishing a highly reliable dual-threat baseline.

His supporting cast is loaded with high-end talent. Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland are incredibly strong playmakers, as is Luther Burden. If Burden can quickly shake his current groin injury, we could realistically be looking at the most dynamic trio of pass catchers in the league paired with a plus-athlete under center.

Defensively, I'm not sold on this Bears unit at all, and that vulnerability could easily result in plenty of favorable, pass-heavy, trailing scripts.

Perhaps the most encouraging part of his fantasy profile is the obvious room for growth. Williams completed just 58.1% of his passes last season and was still a highly valuable weekly asset. That accuracy doesn't even have to become a strength for him to challenge the second tier of fantasy QBs.

If he can simply approach league-average efficiency metrics to pair with his rushing ability, there's a world where Williams is the highest-scoring quarterback not named Josh Allen in 2026. Draft him confidently as a high-end starter.

The juice is worth the squeeze here and this is going to be a name I'm circling with regularity in the DFS streets. We saw proof of concept a season ago and we've seen this story before where a Johnson led offense evolves with time and becomes elite.

Everyone knows what the Bears did last season and yet, I still think there is a chance to hop on this bandwagon before it truly takes off!

articles.title: LSU poised to sign former NFL players after SEC says it will comply with court order
articles.summary: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris are expected to sign with the Tigers.
articles.body:
LSU may soon fire the loudest shot yet in a battle with its own conference.

The SEC has communicated to plaintiff attorneys that the league will comply with a Louisiana state court order permitting their clients — former professional football players — from a return to college. Yahoo Sports obtained a message from the conference legal counsel to attorneys signaling the news.

The message paves the way for a host of players to join SEC programs, most notably at LSU , where two players who signed pro contracts this summer are poised to now be on coach Lane Kiffin's roster.

Dae'Quan Wright, the former Ole Miss tight end who signed an undrafted free agent contract with the Cleveland Browns, and Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris, who signed with the Saints before being waived, plan to sign with the university. While the signing does not immediately constitute a violation of the SEC's new policy banning former professional players, their inclusion on LSU's final roster would. Rosters are not set until a day before the first game.

The impending signings continues to put at odds the SEC and LSU in an unprecedented legal collision over athlete eligibilit y that's been brewing for days. A Louisiana judge earlier this month granted Wright and other players an additional year of eligibility through a temporary restraining order by prohibiting the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility standards.

The move created a whirlwind of a week where all the power conferences adopted their own eligibility policy banning pro athletes from returning to college. And then, on Friday, a Baton Rouge judge granted a request from players' attorneys to also enjoin the SEC's new rule, amending the complaint to add the league and commissioner Greg Sankey as defendants.

It's not only football. RJ Luis, a basketball standout who played three games in the NBA and was part of two franchises, is a commitment to Will Wade's hoops team .

The addition of all three players violated two SEC policies: the ban on pro players and the prohibition on players moving from one conference member to another outside of the transfer portal window. Each violation comes with stiff sanctions, including a half-season suspension of the head coach, a 50% fine of a school's athletic budget and the forfeiture of voting privileges.

However, the Louisiana judge's order prohibits the league from enforcing sanctions against a school, coach or athlete. A preliminary injunction hearing — where the judge determines if the restraining order will be more permanent until a trial — is scheduled for Thursday in Baton Rouge.

Two days later, LSU hosts Clemson in a top-25 game in Tiger Stadium in coach Lane Kiffin's debut.

LSU isn't necessarily alone in intentionally leaving open roster spots for pro players and/or those transferring within the league outside of the portal window. Texas has a player, Cole Hutson, who participated in minicamp with two NFL teams, received a state injunction and is practicing with the Longhorns. Kentucky is expected to sign former Missouri players Mark Mitchell, who played games in the NBA summer league.

But LSU has been the most aggressive, with its brash coach and even the Louisiana governor leading the way.

In a news conference on Monday, Kiffin said the players suing the NCA were "wronged" because of the association's timing of the new eligibility policy, suggested that other programs are also recruiting the same athletes and said he's only trying to improve his roster through a "relentless pursuit of excellence."

"That's how I live," he said. "It's how I run the team. And that we're always going to look at every avenue to give you the best team, to give you the best players, so that you have the best chance to win."

The state's governor, Jeff Landry, released a statement to Front Office Sports earlier this week on the issue, blaming the system and not his state school: "Don't hate the player; hate the game."

More players are available outside of the Louisiana suit.

A Dallas judge on Thursday granted additional eligibility to more than two-dozen athletes playing multiple sports — a complaint filed, like the Louisiana one, by attorney Ryan Downton and the Texas Trial Lawyers. Downton represented former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia in a case in 2024 that opened the floodgates for many eligibility lawsuits against the association.

But the latest wave of cases stems from the NCAA's new eligibility policy enacted this summer. The new rule grants athletes five seasons of eligibility, up from four under the previous bylaw. The association chose not to make an exception for players graduating this spring who exhausted their eligibility under the former policy.

That decision, made by the member schools themselves, sparked the current landscape: more than 300 athletes filing 60-plus lawsuits for an additional year, including those who this spring signed pro contracts without knowledge of the NCAA's rule change. Athletes have won a wide portion of those rulings, but inconsistent judicial decisions — the NCAA has, for now, won cases in Ohio, New York, Nevada and a federal suit in Colorado — has created an uneven competitive playing field.

"The 'chaos' of NFL players going back to college is a one-time occurrence specifically resulting from the NCAA arbitrarily denying Class of 2022 athletes from having a fifth year under its new rule, which the NCAA forecasted was coming for a long time," Florida-based sports lawyer Darren Heitner, who's assisting with the lawsuit and represents some of the players involved, posted online earlier this week.

"They wouldn't have been NFL players at all if the NCAA would have rightfully given them an extra year. Alternatively, had the NCAA provided the option of a fifth year and the athlete still went to the NFL, the player wouldn't be allowed to go back to college. But that's not what happened."

Judges are not only granting athletes eligibility but creating temporary windows for them to transfer and permitting pro players to return to college — a long-honored college policy that is now under attack, in part because of the monetary incentive. Pro athletes cut from rosters are expected to receive big paydays at their colleges through NIL and revenue-share agreements.

The act of schools accepting professional players is emerging as a seminal moment in the industry, as college executives rally to halt the action. Within a matter of 48 hours, leaders of the Big Ten, SEC, Big 12 and ACC adopted their own pro-player bans in an effort to evade legal challenges by governing a smaller group of schools than the hundreds under the NCAA umbrella. But despite unanimous votes from school presidents to pass such rules, universities are leaving open roster spots and are, privately, supporting players in legal battles — most notably LSU, which played a role in the Louisiana filing.

The situation has sprung to life the industry and its legion of fans, many of whom do not publicly support the return of pro athletes.

College Football Playoff leaders may soon follow the power leagues, in fact. They plan next week to seriously discuss and possibly adopt a participation policy that disqualifies several categories of athletes, including those who have previously signed pro contracts, sources with knowledge of the talks told Yahoo Sports.

But plaintiff attorneys believe that these athletes belonging to the 2022 high school class should have been granted an additional year of eligibility. On the other side, NCAA and conference officials believe they are taking spots from other players on the eve of the start of the fall sports season.

"Courts across the country granting relief to ineligible athletes who already had every opportunity to compete in college — sometimes without even having a hearing — are failing to appreciate the destabilizing effect their rulings are having on college sports," the NCAA released in a statement earlier this month. "The lawyers bringing these cases seemingly won't be satisfied until every professional athlete can treat college sports as a fallback option, regardless of the opportunities it strips from both those who will never have a chance to begin their collegiate sports experience and those who are currently on campus working out with the team and attending classes."

articles.title: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton: James Tarkowski's late goal denies Bournemouth victory on Marco Rose's home debut
articles.summary: Match report and free highlights as James Tarkowski scores late on to deny Bournemouth victory; Alex Scott gave Bournemouth the lead just before half-time but Tarkowski's goal in stoppage time earned the visitors a hard-fought point
articles.body:
Alex Scott's sublime finish just before half-time put Bournemouth in front and they looked on course to take all three points before Tarkowski fired home an Everton equaliser.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Everton

Bournemouth were unchanged from the side that lost to Manchester City on the opening weekend, as James Garner replaced Hayden Hackney to partner Nottingham Forest transfer target Harrison Armstrong in Everton's midfield.

The visitors would have been in front early on but for some heroics from Bournemouth goalkeeper Dorde Petrovic who first saved Jarrad Branthwaite's header from a corner before making another fine stop to deny Iliman Ndiaye.

Pickford did well to deny Rayan at the other end before Petrovic made another stunning double save, first stopping a goal-bound effort from Tyrique George before getting up to make a point-blank save to deny Barry, who should have scored from less than six yards out.

Bournemouth punished the visitors shortly before half-time after some excellent work from Evanilson. The striker turned Tarkowski before cutting the ball across to Scott, who showed remarkable composure to take an extra touch and slot into the far corner.

Barry then missed the target from close range before he was denied again in the second half when Petrovic got down well to save after the striker - who was later replaced by Beto - had been played in by Armstrong.

Bournemouth nearly snatched a second late on, but Evanilson's effort deflected behind.

And they were left to rue that miss when Tarkowski was first to react after Bournemouth failed to clear a corner to smash home a late equaliser.

The key moments from the Vitality Stadium

10: SAVE! Dewsbury-Hall delivers a fine inswinging corner which Branthwaite meets at the near post. His header is going in but Petrovic sticks out an arm and flicks it behind for another corner. What a save!

15: SAVE! Brilliant from Rayan down the right to beat Garner and hold him off before driving into the box. The Brazilian manages to get a shot away from a tight angle but Pickford is there to save with his legs.

17: SAVE! This time it's Ndiaye who forces a smart stop from Petrovic, the Bournemouth goalkeeper diving low to push the ball behind for another Everton corner.

20: PETROVIC WITH A DOUBLE SAVE! First he stops George's effort from the edge of the area, but only by pushing the ball into the path of Barry. Barry should score from a few yards out, but Petrovic is there again!

41: GOAL! Rayan picks up the ball on the edge of his own box and then plays a long pass forward to Evanilson, who turns Tarkowski inside out before finding Scott on the edge of the area. The Bournemouth midfielder then shows real composure, taking one touch to set himself before placing the ball with his right foot into the far corner.

50: SAVE! It's Barry once more who thinks he's scored, but the Bournemouth goalkeeper is there to deny him again.

79: SAVE! Pickford gets down quickly to make a smart stop. The ball lands at the feet of Evanilson, but the Bournemouth striker's close-range effort is somehow deflected behind for a corner.

90+1: GOAL! Hackney's corner is a poor one. It's straight towards Tavernier, but the Bournemouth winger doesn't communicate with Christie and they both challenge for the ball. Neither player clears it properly and it falls to Tarkowski, who powers his effort low along the ground and into the far corner.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Coventry 0-1 Hull: Liam Millar seals second straight victory for the Tigers as Frank Lampard's side lose again
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Liam Millar secures second-straight win for Hull and extends Coventry's wait for a Premier League win; chants of 'we're going to win the league' rang out from the away end as Hull added to their first win against Man Utd with three points
articles.body:
Still high on their opening scalp against Manchester United, after Millar slotted past Carl Rushworth on the break, there were chants of "we're going to win the league" from the away end.

In scoring the winner, Millar, who replaced Elliot Stroud in the second half, made up for an earlier miss on the counter where he dragged a big chance wide of the target.

Latest news and rumours: Coventry | Hull

Coventry failed to mark their first home game in the Premier League for 25 years with a victory, but looked the more likely side when new signing Taiwo Awoniyi was denied by Konstantinos Tzolakis in the first half. Awoniyi made a nuisance of himself in his first Premier League start for the Sky Blues after scoring in a 4-2 win over Plymouth in the Carabao Cup in midweek. But it wasn't enough.

Instead, Coventry spurned a huge opportunity to avenge their defeat to Champions Arsenal in the curtain-raiser in what was dubbed a 'relegation six-pointer'. It was a baptism of fire on the opening day for Lampard's side, but as the Championship winners, against the play-off winners, the chance to take at least a point was invaluable.

Coventry's 25-year wait for a Premier League win continues.

The key moments from the Coventry Building Society Arena

21: CHANCE! Hull fail to clear their lines and the ball eventually rolls to Yerenkyi, who finds Awoniyi with a cross. Awoniyi meets it, heading right at Tzolakis.

38: BIG CHANCE! Tzolakis denies a sure goal from Awoniyi. The ball is whipped into the area by Tchaouna before falling to the striker. It looked like he knew very little about it as it bounced off his thigh goalwards.

50: SAVE! Rushworth gets across with strong hands to keep out a Mendy's piledriver from range.

57: NEARLY! Coventry fly forward on the counter with Tchaouna set on his way by Rudoni.

74: CHANCE! Millar is played through by McBurnie and has space and time to drive at Amenda, coming in from the right. He checks inside and shoots, dragging the effort wide of the post.

82: GOAL! NO MISTAKING A SECOND TIME! Millar finishes off a Hull counter-attack. It's Belloumi just outside the opposition area that finds the ball at his feet, turning and driving forward before picking out Millar on his left

McBurnie: Man Utd was a free hit - this was more important

Hull City's Oli McBurnie speaking to Sky Sports:

"It suits us the longer the game goes on at 0-0. We're at their place. They want to win after their first game so we knew the pressure would be on them. At the end of the day, a 0-0 wouldn't have been the worst result for us.

"The pressure wasn't on us to score. The moment they committed forward, the more space we thought would appear. That was the case, and thankfully Liam stuck one in the net.

"They are all tough in the Premier League; it doesn't get much harder.

Manchester United was a different challenge, last week was a free hit but these games against teams that are so-called around us are more important when it comes to the end of the season.

"They didn't have the best result last week but we know they are a really good team. It's an excellent result for us. As starts go, two from two isn't bad."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Liverpool: Andoni Iraola says fourth official's electronic board issue delayed subs ahead of Nottingham Forest being awarded penalty
articles.summary: Liverpool were frustrated at being unable to make a triple substitution before Nottingham Forest were awarded a penalty on Saturday, with an electronic board issue meaning they missed three opportunities to make the change in the eventual 2-2 draw
articles.body:
Forest took the lead for the second time in the match on 70 minutes, when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the spot after Neco Williams had been fouled by Alisson.

At that point, Liverpool had been trying to make a triple substitution for over two minutes - during which time the ball had gone out of play on three occasions.

Sub Ryan Gravenberch and Iraola could both be seen gesturing in frustration to the fourth official Tim Robinson, who was squatting down to two electronic boards.

According to official guidance, when substitutions are being made, the process is that the club should complete a subs card and prepare their subs board with the relevant players' numbers and, once ready, then pass this to the fourth official, who will hold it up.

"Definitely he was having some problems with the board or something," said Iraola in his post-match press conference.

Crucially, Williams' run into the box came from a quick throw taken by Liam Delap - who had come on as a sub himself, seconds before Liverpool prepared their triple change.

That was the third occasion the ball had gone out of play after Liverpool's proposed subs had gone to the touchline in readiness to come on.

Each time referee Samuel Barrott allowed play to resume, deeming Liverpool not ready to make their substitutions.

"What would have happened [if the board had been working?]," asked Iraola. "Definitely you stop because I want to sub. It doesn't happen, the quick throw-in, because we are waiting for the subs."

Liverpool's three subs - Gravenberch, Rio Ngumoha and Kostas Tzimikas - eventually came on after Gibbs-White had scored the penalty.

Liverpool went on to score an 82nd-minute equaliser through Victor Munoz but Iraola remains winless as Reds boss after two Premier League matches.

65:23 - Nottingham Forest's Liam Delap comes on for Dan Ndoye.

65:43 - Three Liverpool subs go to the touchline in preparation to come on.

66:23 - The ball goes out of play for a Forest throw-in.

One of Liverpool's three prepared subs, Gravenberch gestures towards the fourth official in frustration, with the fourth official squatting down beside two electronic boards. Iraola then speaks to the fourth official, with his arms out, seemingly asking what is going on.

It is reported by commentators that Iraola has changed who he wants to come off - deciding to leave Jeremie Frimpong on but to take off Mac Allister instead.

67:11 - The ball goes out for another Forest throw-in.

The fourth official is still squatting beside the electronic boards, trying to get them to work. Iraola gestures with his arms stretched out wide to ask why the delay to the subs is continuing.

67:38 - The ball goes out for another Forest throw-in. Delap takes it quickly to Williams to send him into the Liverpool penalty area.

67:46 - Forest are awarded a penalty when Williams is fouled by Alisson.

69:51 - Gibbs-White scores the penalty to put Forest 2-1 up.

Iraola: I don't see the reason why it happened

"I can't explain because I don't have an explanation.

"I wanted to make those three subs three minutes before. There have been two, three, four times I think the ball has gone out and I still don't know the reason why we haven't made the subs.

"Definitely he was having some problems with the board or something.

"What would have happened? Definitely you stop because I want to sub. It doesn't happen, the quick throw-in because we are waiting for the subs.

"If I ask for the sub - and I'd already asked and I complained the previous time the ball went out and the supporters, I think they were shouting, everyone was aware of the situation.

"But I don't [know] the reason why it happened.

"The penalty, I leave you to decide if it's a penalty or not."

articles.title: Celtic 2-1 Falkirk: Camilo Duran's double earns Scottish Premiership win to ease Hoops' Champions League heartache
articles.summary: Report as Celtic beat Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership; Camilo Duran scored a first-half double; Colby Donovan's own-goal pulled one back for the visitors; the Hoops have won their opening three league games; Falkirk remain winless
articles.body:
After throwing away a four-goal lead to crash out of Europe's elite competition, Martin O'Neill had told his players to show their true "character" against Falkirk.

The players emerged to a banner reading "world-class embarrassment" but Camilo Duran soon had the Hoops support cheering when he pounced on a horrible mistake by Bairns goalkeeper Scott Bain to put them in front.

The Colombian striker then turned Kieran Tierney's cross into the net to double Celtic's lead before the break.

Benjamin Nygren passed up a number of chances to put the hosts further in front and Colby Donovan put the ball in his own net after Jacob Murrell was denied by Viljami Sinisalo to make the final period more nervy than it should have been.

Celtic were without captain Callum McGregor and Kasper Hogh through injury as they made it three wins from three in the Scottish Premiership. John McGlynn's Bairns remain without a victory in the league.

1: CHANCE! Falkirk with an early chance, but Carter-Vickers diverts the ball past before Parkinson can tap in.

4: GOAL CELTIC! A terrible mistake from former Hoops goalkeeper Bain gifting Duran the opener, given after a VAR check.

29: GOAL CELTIC! Tierney's cross finds Duran unmarked, and he sweeps the ball into the bottom corner.

33: OVER! Nygren gets on the end of a cross, but he sends his header over the crossbar.

34: OVER! It's Nygren again. He bursts into the box, but strikes over the bar.

38: SAVE! Nygren tries again, but he is denied by the Falkirk keeper who pushes it over the bar.

48: CHANCE! Parkinson brings down the ball in the box, turns and fires over the bar.

50: SAVE! Bain denies Nygren at close range after a lovely pass from Oxlade-Chamberlain.

52: OVER! Nygren again! This time a curling shot from just inside the box, which is inches over the bar.

72: GOAL FALKIRK! Murrell's low shot is saved by Sinisalo, only for Donovan to put the ball into his own net.

65: OVER! Scales heads over from Yang's cross as Celtic look to restore their two-goal lead.

76: CHANCE! Nygren sends the ball high over the bar - Baur is fuming, believing he should have left it for him.

86: SAVE! Osmand's low effort is straight into the arms of Bain.

articles.title: Norwich 4-1 Burnley: Mohamed Toure and Andre Brooks both net twice in romp
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Norwich City and Burnley at Carrow Road on Saturday; Mo Toure and Andre Brooks both score twice as the Canaries cruise to victory.
articles.body:
The Canaries never looked back after scoring twice in the opening five minutes, with two goals apiece from Mo Toure and new boy Andre Brooks guiding them to a welcome win, after being beaten in their opening two league games.

It was another disappointing afternoon for Burnley, however, summed up late on when Josh Laurent, who had scored their consolation goal, was dismissed for a second bookable offence.

The Clarets have taken just one point from their first three fixtures under new boss Nicky Hayen - and remain without a league victory since winning at Crystal Palace in the Premier League back in February.

Norwich took advantage of some woeful defending to swiftly move two up at a soggy Carrow Road.

With less than 90 seconds on the clock, Anel Ahmedhodzic somehow contrived to miss a routine ball forward from Jose Cordoba, allowing Toure to run through and finish emphatically.

The Canaries doubled their advantage in their next attack, with Kenny McLean's clever pass giving an unmarked Anthony Musaba the chance to deliver a low cross for Brooks to convert.

It got even worse for the Clarets on 21 minutes as Norwich made it 3-0.

This time time the visitors were unable to deal with an Oscar Schwartau corner from the right, with the ball dropping kindly for Toure to grab his second of the afternoon from close range.

Burnley looked shell-shocked, having twice gone close to pulling one back through first Zian Flemming and then Aaron Ramsey.

But they did manage to get the goal their attacking play merited on 27 minutes when Kyle Walker slipped the ball inside for Laurent to fire home off a post from just outside the box.

The Clarets came desperately close to pulling another one back three minutes after the interval, with Jacob Bruun Larsen's piledriver coming back off the upright.

The visitors were still very much in the game at that stage but they failed to make their territorial dominance count and were made to pay when the Canaries made it 4-1 on 67 minutes.

Some excellent approach play was rewarded as substitute Papa Diallo spread the ball wide to Jack Stacey, who crossed for Brooks to double his tally for the day and end any hope of a comeback.

Burnley suffered more misery in 77th minute when they were reduced to 10 men as Laurent was shown a second yellow for hauling back Anis Ben Slimane as the Norwich substitute attempted to break forward.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Watford 1-1 West Ham: Mattie Pollock own goal earns point for Hammers
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and West Ham United at Vicarage Road on Saturday; Hammers underwhelming start to the season continues as they are held to a goalless draw by the Hornets.
articles.body:
The Hammers were booed off by a large section of their travelling support, who serenaded their under-pressure manager with a chorus of 'You're getting sacked in the morning' despite a dominant second-half display.

The Hammers are struggling to live up to their billing as Championship promotion favourites after letting a two-goal lead slip at Burnley and a shock home defeat by Charlton.

Here they fell behind to a brilliant goal from Watford's 19-year-old prospect Amin Nabizada and West Ham needed a freakish equaliser, from a dreadful mistake, to earn a point.

Nuno handed a League debut to 18-year-old defender Airidas Golambeckis, who was composed and assured.

But the Hammers had already survived Nabizada curling narrowly wide when the Hornets went in front after 19 minutes in spectacular fashion.

The Afghanistan international appeared to be crowded out in the box but he summoned the impudence to dink an exquisite, curling chip beyond Mads Hermansen and into the far corner.

It was a goal reminiscent of Gerard Deulofeu's trick shot at Wembley in the Hornets' FA Cup semi-final comeback against Wolves seven years ago, and West Ham were briefly rattled.

But when the East-enders rattled the collection tin, Hornets defender Kevin Keben gave generously.

Trying to shepherd the ball along the dead-ball line towards his own goal, Keben was robbed by Taty Castellanos and home skipper Mattie Pollock turned the ball into his own net from point-blank range.

The comical nature of the equaliser drained the early swagger from Watford and Keben's confidence evaporated for a time, although he did well to recover his composure later.

As West Ham warmed to their task after the interval, Arne Engels fired narrowly wide and only Pollock's last-ditch tackle thwarted Manor Solomon.

Much as they were on top, however, the Hammers still lived on their nerves and only Joel Veltman's critical deflection over the top denied Iker Bravo a late winner on a rare Hornets breakaway.

And much as Watford were forced back for most of the second half, they deserved their point to preserve head coach Alessio Dionisi's unbeaten start in the Championship.

Dionisi has been operating with such slender resources that he named two goalkeepers on the bench. He was well satisfied with the response to his weakened side's 5-1 hammering by league One Peterborough in the Carabao Cup in midweek.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Blackburn 1-2 QPR: Paul Smyth and Jimmy Dunne net in comeback win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Blackburn Rovers and Queens Park Rangers at Ewood Park on Saturday; Paul Smyth and Jimmy Dunne score as Julien Stephan's side earn second-half comeback win.
articles.body:
After an even first half, Rovers took a 49th-minute lead through Ryoya Morishita's spectacular volley, but the visitors hit back within two minutes through Paul Smyth's composed finish and they deservedly completed the turnaround in the 74th minute through Jimmy Dunne's powerful header.

Julian Stephan's side showed impressive character to recover from that setback and sit with seven points from a possible nine, which moves them fourth in the league at this early stage.

Blackburn's own unbeaten run came to an end and though the effort could never be questioned, Tony Mowbray's men simply lacked the depth of options off the bench compared to their opponents.

Despite QPR's accomplished start, Rovers carved out the first clear opening in the 21st minute when Ryan Alebiosu raided down the right. His cross was perfect for Todd Cantwell at the back post but he guided his free header over the bar.

The same two players combined nine minutes later to go even closer when Alebiosu's centre missed everybody and Cantwell showed terrific technique to step back before unleashing an effort on the bounce that whistled just past the far post.

QPR should have gone ahead when Rumarn Burrell slipped Ilias Chair in, only for Balazs Toth's outstretched left leg to deny him.

Ronnie Edwards forced another fine save from Toth as the break approached, the goalkeeper going full-stretch to tip away the curling 20-yard shot destined for the bottom right corner.

Blackburn broke the deadlock in stunning fashion at the start of the second half when Andri Gudjohnsen's flick-on found Morishita, who controlled and let fly with an astonishing left-foot volley that flew into the top corner from 20 yards.

QPR's response was swift as Burrell raced down the right and delivered an intelligent low cross that found Smyth at the near post, who expertly guided the ball beyond Toth.

A superb reflex save from Charles prevented Rovers regaining the lead in the 53rd minute when he got down low to flick Alebiosu's cross away.

But from there, QPR exerted their dominance as Burrell glanced a 64th-minute header wide and further chances came and went when substitute Kwame Poku directed Burrell's left-wing cross wide, and Edwards flashed another piledriver past the post.

Their pressure deservedly told 16 minutes from the end when QPR recycled the ball following a clearance and Tariq Lamptey's superb cross put the ball on a plate for Dunne to power his header home from close range.

Alfie Lloyd saw a late shot blocked but QPR eased to a second consecutive win at Ewood Park.

articles.title: Bolton 0-1 Lincoln: Ben House scores Imps winner as they claim first win of the season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton Wanderers and Lincoln City at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on Saturday; Ben House scores the only goal as Imps claim their first second-tier win in 65 years.
articles.body:
The Imps had lost their opening two Championship fixtures against Middlesbrough and Portsmouth.

But after Wanderers had failed to unlocked City's defensive door, House stole in to earn the visitors their first three points at this level since April 1961.

Keeper George Wickens was Lincoln's other hero as he repelled a succession of efforts as Bolton looked to build on an opening-day win over Preston and battling draw at QPR.

Wanderers and their visitors played out two draws last season en route to their respective promotions.

This latest meeting was similarly even in the early exchanges. Bolton dominated possession with the best chances falling to striker Sam Dalby.

He was inches away from connecting with Lewis Brunt's teasing cross from the Lincoln left.

And the former Wrexham man was even closer after 22 minutes, sliding onto full debutant Samuel Iling-Junior's cross and striking the outside of Wickens' upright.

Matchwinner House miskicked when Colin McGrandles and Callum Elder fashioned a decent shooting opportunity and then collected a booking for diving under goalie Jack Bonham's challenge.

Bolton continued to dominate and Wickens denied Brunt his first Trotters' goal with a fingertip save from the defender's header.

John McAtee was also foiled by the Imps' keeper, Dalby headed over and former Lincoln midfielder Ethan Erhahon side footed narrowly wide as Jack Bonham remained untested at the other end.

Elder scuffed a rare effort wide as Lincoln started the second half with greater purpose.

They went even closer after 50 minutes as Ivan Varfolomeev forced Bonham into his opening save as Josh Sheehan was dispossessed and referee Ben Speedie ignored appeals for a foul.

Bolton made a double substitution just after the hour with Iling-Junior and Akin Famewo replaced by Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal. Lincoln responded by bringing on Rob Street for Freddie Draper and two minutes later made the breakthrough.

Elder's long throw travelled through to House who stole in to head home from close range.

Dong certainly pepped up Wanderers' attack, forcing Wickens into a save and then seeing another shot blocked. Dalby bundled another effort the wrong side of a post as Lincoln held firm.

Bolton mastered the art of late goals last season and substitute Ryan Hardie almost provided an equaliser. Again though Wickens reacted smartly to a this latest close-range attempt.

And he was still defying Bolton in stoppage time, tipping away Sheehan's 20-yard free kick to secure Lincoln's first ever victory at the Toughsheet Community Stadium and first away win in Bolton in 42 years.

articles.title: Charlton 1-0 Preston: Karlan Grant scores winner as Addicks maintain perfect start
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Preston North End at The Valley on Saturday; Karlan Grant nets the only goal as Nathan Jones Addicks make it three wins from three.
articles.body:
Karlan Grant's first goal for the Addicks since rejoining on a free transfer from West Brom ensured that the south Londoners are the only side in the division still boasting a 100 per cent record.

It is the first time that Charlton have won their opening three matches in the second tier since the 1992-93 campaign.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones made just one change from last weekend's win at West Ham with Ivan Mesik replacing Billy Koumetio, who suffered a hamstring injury in the heavy midweek Carabao Cup loss to Tottenham.

The visitors named new signings Stanley Mills and Caleb Wiley on the bench.

The opening 45 minutes was desperately short on quality with Charlton struggling to find space against organised opposition.

North End had the first clear-cut chance after 30 minutes but Callum Lang was unable to keep his header down from Andrija Vukcevic's left-wing delivery.

Addicks goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo, making his first home appearance after signing on loan from Wrexham, did not have a save to make before the break.

Charlton defender Amari'i Bell produced excellent defending to snuff out the threat of Lang after he initially managed to roam goalside of the Jamaica international.

Charlton finally threatened in the 37th minute. Miles Leaburn produced a brave header from a cross by Tyreece Campbell which went narrowly past the left post.

Grant had the last shooting opportunity in first-half stoppage time but his 30-yard free-kick failed to call Preston keeper Daniel Iversen into action.

Okonkwo had to be switched on to produce a block to deny Delano Burgzorg early in the second period.

Harry Clarke, who spent the second half of last season on loan with Charlton from Ipswich, sent a right-footed effort harmlessly into the Jimmy Seed Stand shortly before the Addicks took a 56th-minute lead.

Grant squeezed a low shot past Iversen after cutting back inside the penalty area to get a better angle from substitute Millenic Alli's ball to his feet.

Preston centre-back Liam Lindsay could only flick over from six yards out after being found by captain Lewis Gibson.

Charlton continued to threaten a second and Leaburn blazed over while substitute Alan Mwamba had a goalbound shot blocked.

Referee Tom Reeves failed to spot Grant's shot striking the arm of Harry Clarke inside the penalty area as the contest headed into stoppage time.

Alli forced Iversen to plunge to his left to push away a fiercely struck effort.

Preston boss Paul Heckingbottom brought on Mills for his debut in the closing stages but he was unable to make any impact.

North End have lost all three of their Championship matches and badly lacked any spark in SE7.
